    Canonical maps between interval representations #

    For intervals U, V of I_*, the formula f ↦ (t ↦ [t ∈ U] f) defines a morphism k_U ⟶ k_V as soon as, for s ≤ t with t ∈ V and s ∈ U, one has t ∈ U ↔ s ∈ V. This covers the canonical quotient maps a_{ji} : A j ⟶ A i, p_{ji} : P j ⟶ P i and c_i : P i ⟶ Y, and the inclusion b_i : A i ⟶ P i of the manuscript (diagram (2.1)). We also show that 0 → A i → P i → Y → 0 is short exact (Lemma 2.1).
